prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

You are reviewing layouts of one table, all rendered in a real browser with identical content, font, padding and colours; only column widths differ. You do not know who or what produced them. The first image is the content overview (every cell on one line).
Table: [val][adversarial] Long group header over tiny sub-columns (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Merged cells: "Model" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Benchmark accuracy on he" spans 3 col × 1 row; "Notes" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Model" · longest unbreakable word 39px · one-line width 39px
  col 2: header "Benchmark accuracy on held-out multilingual evaluation suite › EN" · longest unbreakable word 18px · one-line width 18px
  col 3: header "Benchmark accuracy on held-out multilingual evaluation suite › ZH" · longest unbreakable word 19px · one-line width 19px
  col 4: header "Benchmark accuracy on held-out multilingual evaluation suite › AR" · longest unbreakable word 18px · one-line width 18px
  col 5: header "Notes" · longest unbreakable word 56px · one-line width 514px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 446px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 445px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Rate EACH layout independently: "excellent" | "good" | "acceptable" | "poor" | "bad", with a short reason that points at what you see. Then name the best layout(s) (ties allowed), say how confident you are (low/medium/high), and note anything you are unsure about.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"","why":""},"B":{"grade":"","why":""},"C":{"grade":"","why":""},"D":{"grade":"","why":""},"E":{"grade":"","why":""},"F":{"grade":"","why":""}},"best":["letter"],"confidence":"","unsure":""}

log.raw: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"good","why":"The notes have room to read comfortably and the language columns are balanced, though the group header wraps to four lines."},"B":{"grade":"good","why":"The group header fits in three lines and the language columns are even, but the narrower notes column makes the first row four lines tall."},"C":{"grade":"good","why":"The header and notes are readable, with balanced language columns; the first note takes four lines."},"D":{"grade":"good","why":"The group header fits neatly in three lines, and the language columns are balanced, though the first note needs four lines."},"E":{"grade":"bad","why":"The notes column is extremely narrow, breaking the first note into many short lines and making its row disproportionately tall."},"F":{"grade":"excellent","why":"The group header and first note each fit in three lines, while the language columns remain balanced and easy to compare."}},"best":["F"],"confidence":"high","unsure":"B, C and D are very similar; their small differences in column width have little effect on readability."}
